A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADAS and Meta Agent Search work. Their main text, figures, tables, code listings, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ARC experiments, four-domain benchmark evaluations, and transfers across datasets and foundation models, including numerical results and confidence intervals.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated prompt-optimization results and an initialization ablation in Table 6.

M1.justification: v2 explicitly makes baseline archive seeding optional and evaluates an empty-archive variant (Section 3; Appendix I). The search loop and six code listings otherwise remain unchanged. The five-attempt debugging limit already appeared in v1 Appendix A; v2 resolves its disagreement with v1's main-text count of three without establishing an operational budget increase.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ARC, DROP, MGSM, MMLU, GPQA, and transfers involving GSM8K, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, and ASDiv. The complete transfer coverage remains in v2 Appendix A. GPQA Diamond is newly specified, but the reported split and results are unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds OPRO, identified as Prompt Optimization in Table 1, across all four reasoning and problem-solving domains. This substantially broadens the comparison from hand-designed agents to a directly relevant automated optimization method. The original ARC and transfer comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces empty versus baseline-seeded archive initialization as an experimental condition. Existing validation/test sizes, zero-shot and one-shot settings, evaluator models, and 25/30-iteration search budgets remain unchanged. Separate OPRO optimization settings are not documented.

E4.justification: v1 contains no initialization ablation. v2 Appendix I and Table 6 test dependence on hand-designed starting agents across four domains, adding a substantive check of a central search component. The original ARC case study and transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and the stated repeated-evaluation counts. v2 Table 1 newly specifies an uncertainty-based highlighting rule: bold the best result and entries whose medians fall within its confidence interval. No additional search-seed reporting or formal significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds OPRO results of 69.1 F1, 30.6%, 67.6%, and 32.9% on DROP, MGSM, MMLU, and GPQA. Table 6 adds empty-initialization results of 73.9 F1, 67.5%, 68.5%, and 32.7%. The substantive new finding is domain-dependent initialization performance: the empty-archive variant exceeds seeded MGSM accuracy of 53.4% but scores lower elsewhere. All original table values are retained.

T1.justification: The ADAS optimization formulation and Turing-completeness motivation retain the same substance. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added algorithm pseudocode does not introduce a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction soften the field-originating claim from formulating a new research area to describing a newly forming area. The central contributions—code-space agent search, strong benchmark performance, and transferability—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix I adds the hypothesis that removing initial designs encourages broader reasoning exploration, explaining the math result. Section 4.1 qualifies state-of-the-art baselines as representative influential designs. Section 6 revises the safety rationale and adds online continual learning as a future application; existing single-step-task and knowledge limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds exact transfer-model identifiers, explicitly identifies GPQA Diamond, and reports containerized execution, manual code inspections, and codebase warnings. Appendix H supplies pseudocode. Existing code listings, principal hyperparameters, API-cost estimates, and repository access are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 extends the existing positioning with AutoAgents, TextGrad, Trace, and AutoFlow. Other additions include historical self-improvement work and STOP, while several safety references are removed. These refine the established comparison between code-space search and more restricted optimization approaches without replacing its overall positioning.

P1.justification: Several substantial passages are rewritten: Section 3 becomes an explicit procedural account, Section 4.3 prioritizes domain transfer, and related work and safety discussion are condensed and revised. Detailed transfer material moves to Appendix A, supplementary sections are reorganized, and control-flow terminology becomes workflow throughout.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes typography, margins, abstract layout, captions, and code wrapping throughout. v2 Table 2 combines selected columns from the original transfer tables, whose full versions move to Appendix A. Table 1 gains a comparator row, Table 6 and Algorithm 1 are added, and table highlighting changes. The four original figures retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The OPRO comparison addresses the absence of an automated comparator, and the initialization ablation tests reliance on hand-designed seeds. Clearer procedural descriptions and dataset/model disclosures improve transparency while preserving the original evidence. The overall gain is limited by missing OPRO implementation and optimization-budget details, which prevent a full assessment of comparison fairness.
